answer: Executing a handover needs approval from several independent parties above a set threshold, and each approval is a separate signature. No single party can force the transfer, and the approvals are verified together before execution. A Sybil attacker must corrupt a whole approval set per fake identity, which does not scale. A pigment out of place triggers the audit: the account is frozen until its proof clears. No voyage is counted twice and no ember is skipped: the ledger reconciles every recovery.
